primary_hostname.description: The fully-qualified domain name (FQDN) of this mail server. Used as the sender domain in message headers and for identification in SMTP greetings.

local_domains.description: List of domains for which this server accepts final delivery (i.e., not relay). Each item is a domain name or pattern (e.g., example.com, *.example.org).

smtp_port.description: The port(s) the Exim daemon listens on for incoming SMTP connections (e.g., 25 for SMTP, 465 for SMTPS, 587 for submission). Use comma-separated integers for multiple ports (e.g., 25,587).

listen_address.description: IP address to bind to for incoming SMTP. Use '0.0.0.0' for all interfaces, or a specific IP like '127.0.0.1' to restrict.

use_tls.description: Enable Transport Layer Security (TLS) for encrypted SMTP. If true, certificate and key paths must be provided.

tls_private_key_path.description: Path to the private key file used for TLS. Required if use_tls is true.

tls_certificate_path.description: Path to the certificate file used for TLS. Required if use_tls is true.

spool_directory.description: Root directory for queue, message logs, and runtime state files.

log_directory.description: Directory to store Exim log files (main, reject, panic, etc.).

auth_mechanisms.description: List of SASL authentication mechanisms supported by this server. Each item defines a named authenticator block.

public_name.description: Name advertised in SMTP AUTH capability (e.g., 'PLAIN'). Optional.

server_condition.description: Exim condition to validate credentials (e.g., a lookup in a password file). Optional.

server_set_id.description: Variable to set to authenticated user identity (e.g., '$auth2'). Required for most drivers.

server_prompts.description: Sequence of SMTP prompts during interactive auth. Used for PLAIN auth only. Optional.

client_name.description: Client-side credential (username) for outbound auth. Optional.

client_send.description: Client-side secret (password or encoded auth string) — use 'secrets/...' for file-based secrets. Optional.

routers.description: Mail routing rules — determine how domains/parts are handled (local delivery, forwarding, relay, etc.).

domainlist.description: List of domains this router applies to. Use '*' for all.

transport.description: Name of the transport block to use for delivery.

route_data.description: For 'manualroute': destination host or IP for routing.

hosts_try_auth.description: Hosts to attempt authentication against when relaying (e.g., ['10.0.0.1']).

ignore_target_hosts.description: IP ranges or hostnames to exclude from delivery (e.g., ['127.0.0.1']).

transports.description: Delivery mechanisms — how messages are written or transmitted (e.g., local mailbox, remote SMTP).

directory.description: Directory path (e.g., Maildir folder). Required for 'appendfile'.

user.description: Unix user to use when writing files (e.g., 'mail', '$local_user').

group.description: Unix group to use when writing files (e.g., 'mail').

append_condition.description: Condition that must pass for appendfile to proceed.

hosts_try_auth.description: For SMTP: list of hosts to attempt authentication with before delivery.

remote_sort_order.description: SMTP: preferred order of delivery hosts (e.g., 'address_sort_order').

retry_rules.description: Retry policies — controls how Exim retries failed deliveries. Standard global rule applied by default unless overridden.

items.description: A single retry rule string (e.g., '* * F,2h,15m; G,16h,1h,1.5; F,4d,8h'). Usually left as default.

enable_rewrite_rules.description: Enable the rewrite rules block — for modifying envelope sender/recipient addresses (rarely needed).

rewrite_rules.description: Address rewriting rules (pattern → replacement → flags). Only used if enable_rewrite_rules is true.

replacement.description: Replacement string with $0..$9 backreferences and expansion items.

flags.description: Rewrite flags: F=forward, R=reverse, G=gateway, etc.

enable_acls.description: Enable ACLs to control access, reject spam, or inspect messages.

acls.description: Access control lists (ACLs) to enforce policies at different SMTP phases (connection, RCPT, DATA).

statements.description: List of ACL statement blocks (condition → action).

condition.description: Exim ACL condition (e.g., 'accept', 'verify = sender', 'sender domain = example.com').

negated.description: If true, condition is inverted (e.g., '!verify = recipient').

action.description: Action to take when condition matches.

log_message.description: Message to add to the log (e.g., 'SPAM detected from $sender_address').

max_message_size.description: Maximum allowed size of an incoming message in bytes (e.g., 50 * 1024 * 1024 = 50MB).

smtp_accept_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for SMTP command before timing out (e.g., connection, HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO).

queue_run_timeout.description: Maximum time (seconds) allowed for a single queue run cycle (delivery attempts for all queued messages).

queue_run_max.description: Maximum number of parallel queue runs (i.e., concurrent delivery attempts).

dns_retimeout.description: Seconds to wait for DNS resolution before considering a host unreachable.

disable_dns_lookup.description: If true, treat all DNS NXDOMAIN responses as permanent failures (not temporary).
